title: AI-Generated Unhinged Wealthy Family Short Dramas: Who's Watching These Viral, Over-the-Top Stories?
key_facts: AI-generated "family inheritance" short dramas have spread across Douyin, Xiaohongshu and Kuaishou, with everyday objects (wood ear fungi, manicured nails, chopsticks, iPhones) playing rich families.
The plot is one fixed template, usually titled "The Heir of the XX Family"; only the protagonist object changes, and prompt templates exist so AI fills in the blanks.
TopKlout says the absurdity attracts algorithm traffic, but viewers complain about padded plots and one never-revealed suspense point.
Douyin data on native AI short dramas: 221,900 new ones from January to June 2026, 1,055 of them above 100 million views, 515.738 billion new views in total.

Examples of stories with real characters doing far better: "The Laid-off Girl" over 200 million views; another drama made in a bedroom 4.1 billion views; one made by one person for over 10,000 yuan earned 400,000 yuan in revenue sharing.
TopKlout argues the template is a transitional form and that memorable stories, not new protagonist objects, are what is rare.
quote_evidence: Recently, AI-generated family inheritance short dramas have flooded users' mobile phones en masse.

According to data on native AI short dramas from Douyin, from January to June 2026, a total of 221,900 new AI short dramas were released, of which 1,055 exceeded 100 million views, with total new views reaching 515.738 billion.
It is more like a transitional form, a product of the gap period where the whole industry has not yet figured out where to go after AI has flattened the threshold of content creation.
why_it_matters_hint: AI has made short drama scripts and clips so cheap that near-identical absurd formulas flood Chinese video apps.
event_date: Not stated (described as recent); Douyin data covers January to June 2026
notes: Read at 36Kr, which republishes an article from the WeChat account TopKlout (written by "77", published with 36Kr authorization); source credited to TopKlout. The conclusion that the trend will fade is the author's opinion.
